purpose: A hold-out set: questions written after the harness was tuned, by authors who never saw its answers, across fields the other sets do not cover.

questions.question: Under Directive 2014/32/EU, as in force on 2026-11-21, how long must a manufacturer keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity after a measuring instrument has been placed on the market?

sources.passage: Manufacturers shall keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the measuring instrument has been placed on the market.

key.item: retention period for technical documentation and EU declaration of conformity
key.answer: 10 years after the measuring instrument has been placed on the market

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may say 10 years after manufacture or 10 years after supply, because other EU product rules use different start points. This passage starts the period when the measuring instrument has been placed on the market.

questions.question: For Directive 2014/35/EU on low-voltage electrical equipment, as in force on 2026-11-21, what alternating-current and direct-current voltage-rating bands define the equipment to which the Directive applies, apart from Annex II exclusions?

sources.passage: This Directive shall apply to electrical equipment designed for use with a voltage rating of between 50 and 1 000 V for alternating current and between 75 and 1 500 V for direct current, other than the equipment and phenomena listed in Annex II.

key.answer: between 50 and 1 000 V for alternating current
between 75 and 1 500 V for direct current

questions.commonly_confused: A common memory answer is 50–1 000 V AC and 75–1 500 V DC without the Annex II carve-out, or the WEEE definition of not exceeding 1 000 V AC and 1 500 V DC. The question asks the scope clause of Directive 2014/35/EU, which includes the Annex II exclusion.

questions.question: Under Regulation (EU) 2017/1369, as in force on 2026-11-21, after the final unit of a model has been placed on the market, how long must the supplier keep information concerning that model in the compliance part of the product database?

sources.passage: After the final unit of a model has been placed on the market, the supplier shall keep the information concerning that model in the compliance part of the product database for a period of 15 years.

key.item: retention period in compliance part of product database

questions.commonly_confused: The tempting answer is 10 years, because many EU product conformity documents are kept for 10 years. This passage is specifically about the compliance part of the energy-labelling product database and states 15 years.

questions.question: Under Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1189, as in force on 2026-11-21, what are the seasonal space heating particulate matter emission limits for automatically stoked boilers and manually stoked boilers?

sources.passage: seasonal space heating emissions of particulate matter shall not be higher than 40 mg/m3 for automatically stoked boilers and not be higher than 60 mg/m3 for manually stoked boilers;

key.item: particulate matter limit, automatically stoked boilers
particulate matter limit, manually stoked boilers

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may swap the two values or quote the nitrogen oxides limits of 200 mg/m3 and 350 mg/m3. The passage ties 40 mg/m3 to automatically stoked boilers and 60 mg/m3 to manually stoked boilers.

questions.question: Under Directive 2012/19/EU on WEEE, as in force on 2026-11-21, what minimum collection rate applies from 2019, expressed either as a share of the average weight of EEE placed on the market in the three preceding years or as a share of WEEE generated?

sources.passage: From 2019, the minimum collection rate to be achieved annually shall be 65 % of the average weight of EEE placed on the market in the three preceding years in the Member State concerned, or alternatively 85 % of WEEE generated on the territory of that Member State.

key.item: minimum collection rate based on EEE placed on market
key.answer: 65 % of the average weight of EEE placed on the market in the three preceding years

key.item: alternative minimum collection rate based on WEEE generated
key.answer: 85 % of WEEE generated on the territory of that Member State

questions.commonly_confused: The tempting wrong answer is 45 % or 4 kg per inhabitant per year, which are earlier or transitional figures in the same Directive. The question asks the rate from 2019, and the passage gives 65 % or alternatively 85 %.

questions.field: EU ecodesign / light sources and control gear

questions.question: For Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2020, as in force on 2026-11-21, a compliance file lists one light source at the maximum permitted standby power and one separate control gear, declared for no-load mode, at the maximum permitted no-load power. What is the combined maximum power of those two standby/no-load states, and what is that combined value in milliwatts?

sources.passage: The standby power Psb of a light source shall not exceed 0,5 W.

The no-load power Pno of a separate control gear shall not exceed 0,5 W. This applies only to separate control gear for which the manufacturer or importer has declared in the technical documentation that it has been designed for no-load mode.

key.item: combined maximum standby/no-load power in milliwatts

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer 0,5 W because both limits are 0,5 W, or may apply the no-load limit to all separate control gear. The question states the control gear is declared for no-load mode, so two separate 0,5 W limits are added: 0,5 W + 0,5 W = 1,0 W = 1000 mW.

questions.field: EU energy efficiency / primary energy target

questions.question: Directive 2012/27/EU states that 2007 projections showed primary energy consumption in 2020 of 1 842 Mtoe and that a 20 % reduction results in 1 474 Mtoe in 2020. Using only those two printed figures, what is the reduction in Mtoe, and what percentage of the projected 1 842 Mtoe is that reduction?

sources.passage: Projections made in 2007 showed a primary energy consumption in 2020 of 1 842 Mtoe. A 20 % reduction results in 1 474 Mtoe in 2020, i.e. a reduction of 368 Mtoe as compared to projections.

The Conclusions of the European Council of 8 and 9 March 2007 emphasised the need to increase energy efficiency in the Union to achieve the objective of saving 20 % of the Union’s primary energy consumption by 2020 compared to projections.

key.item: reduction as a percentage of the projected 1 842 Mtoe

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may simply quote 20 % and omit the arithmetic, or calculate 20 % of 1 474 Mtoe instead of the projected 1 842 Mtoe. The two printed figures give 1 842 − 1 474 = 368 Mtoe, and 368 ÷ 1 842 = 0.1998, about 20 %.

questions.question: For Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/2281, as in force on 2026-11-21, the conversion coefficient is stated as CC = 2,5, and the Annex calculation rule says electricity consumption shall be multiplied by CC of 2,5. If a calculation uses 80 kWh of electricity consumption, what value must be used after applying CC?

sources.passage: ‘conversion coefficient’ (CC) means a coefficient reflecting the estimated 40 % average EU generation efficiency, as established in Annex IV of Directive 2012/27/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council (1); the value of the conversion coefficient shall be CC = 2,5;
For the purposes of the calculations set out in points 3 to 8, consumption of electricity shall be multiplied by the conversion coefficient CC of 2,5;

key.item: 80 kWh of electricity consumption after applying CC

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may divide by 2,5 and answer 32 kWh, or use the 40 % generation efficiency directly. The passages require multiplication: 80 kWh × 2,5 = 200 kWh.

questions.question: For Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2015, as in force on 2026-11-21, when was Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 repealed, and which two specified paragraphs were repealed earlier on 25 December 2019?

sources.passage: Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012 is repealed with effect from 1 September 2021, with the exception of paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4 which are repealed with effect from 25 December 2019.

key.item: general repeal date for Delegated Regulation (EU) No 874/2012

key.answer: paragraph 2 of Article 3 and paragraph 2 of Article 4

questions.commonly_confused: People often quote only 1 September 2021 as the repeal date for the old lamp-labelling rules. The passage has an express exception: Article 3(2) and Article 4(2) were repealed on 25 December 2019.

questions.question: Under Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2020, as in force on 2026-11-21, from what date were Regulations (EC) No 244/2009, (EC) No 245/2009 and (EU) No 1194/2012 repealed?

sources.passage: Regulations (EC) No 244/2009, (EC) No 245/2009 and (EU) No 1194/2012 are repealed with effect from 1 September 2021.

key.item: repeal date for Regulations (EC) No 244/2009, (EC) No 245/2009 and (EU) No 1194/2012

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may quote 25 December 2019 because that date appears in the related energy-labelling repeal, or may assume the older lighting regulations ended when Regulation (EU) 2019/2020 entered into force. The ecodesign repeal passage states 1 September 2021.

questions.field: EU ecodesign framework / transport scope trap
questions.question: A compliance officer asks: under Directive 2009/125/EC, as in force on 2026-11-21, what ecodesign requirement applies to a means of transport for persons or goods? What is the correct answer?

sources.passage: This Directive shall not apply to means of transport for persons or goods.

key.item: ecodesign requirement under Directive 2009/125/EC for means of transport for persons or goods
key.answer: None; Directive 2009/125/EC does not apply to means of transport for persons or goods

questions.commonly_confused: The tempting wrong answer is to look for a product-specific ecodesign limit or implementing measure. The scope clause says the Directive itself does not apply to means of transport for persons or goods.

questions.question: Under Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1781, as in force on 2026-11-21, what minimum energy-efficiency class is set for electric motors with a rated voltage above 1 000 V? What is the correct answer?

sources.passage: Although the environmental impacts of medium voltage motors are relevant, for the time being no classification exists for the energy efficiency of electric motors with a rated voltage above 1 000 V. Once such a classification is developed, the possibility of setting minimum requirements for medium voltage motors should be reassessed.
have a rated voltage U N above 50 V and up to and including 1 000 V;

key.item: minimum energy-efficiency class for motors above 1 000 V
key.answer: No such class is set; no classification exists for the energy efficiency of electric motors with a rated voltage above 1 000 V

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may quote IE2 or IE3 from general motor-efficiency practice. The Regulation says no classification exists above 1 000 V, and the voltage scope passage stops at up to and including 1 000 V.

questions.question: As in force on 2026-11-21, for an offer of securities to the public in the Union with total consideration below EUR 1 000 000 calculated over 12 months, does the EU prospectus regulation apply, and what is the threshold?

sources.passage: Without prejudice to the second subparagraph of this paragraph and to Article 4, this Regulation shall not apply to an offer of securities to the public with a total consideration in the Union of less than EUR 1 000 000, which shall be calculated over a period of 12 months.

key.item: whether the EU prospectus regulation applies to such an offer
key.answer: No, subject to the stated exceptions
less than EUR 1 000 000 total consideration in the Union over a period of 12 months

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may quote the national-law exemption band between EUR 1 000 000 and EUR 8 000 000, or the fewer-than-150-persons exemption. The question asks the EU-level non-application threshold, which is less than EUR 1 000 000 calculated over 12 months.

questions.field: EU batteries / old and new definitions
questions.question: An auditor is updating a battery-classification procedure that still quotes the historical definition in Directive 2006/66/EC. Using the cited texts, what three conditions define a portable battery or accumulator under that Directive, and what weight limit and design/category exclusions define a portable battery under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542?

sources.passage: ‘portable battery or accumulator’ means any battery, button cell, battery pack or accumulator that: (a) is sealed; and (b) can be hand-carried; and (c) is neither an industrial battery or accumulator nor an automotive battery or accumulator;
‘portable battery’ means a battery that is sealed, weighs 5 kg or less, is not designed specifically for industrial use and is neither an electric vehicle battery, an LMT battery, nor an SLI battery;

key.answer: is neither an industrial battery or accumulator nor an automotive battery or accumulator
not designed specifically for industrial use and neither an electric vehicle battery, an LMT battery, nor an SLI battery

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may carry the Directive’s hand-carried test and industrial/automotive exclusions into the Regulation, or apply the Regulation’s 5 kg limit retrospectively to the Directive. The two definitions are different and must be read separately.

questions.question: On the UN page for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, what exact date does the page give for the Declaration being proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in Paris?

sources.passage: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) is a milestone document in the history of human rights. Drafted by representatives with different legal and cultural backgrounds from all regions of the world, the Declaration was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948 (General Assembly resolution 217 A) as a common standard of achievements for all peoples and all nations.

key.item: date proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in Paris

questions.commonly_confused: People often say 1948 without the day, or confuse it with Human Rights Day observance material. The UN page gives the exact date as 10 December 1948.

questions.question: The UN page for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights says the UDHR has been translated into how many languages? Give the wording used on the page, not a rounded number.

sources.passage: It sets out, for the first time, fundamental human rights to be universally protected and it has been translated into over 500 languages.

key.item: number of languages into which the UDHR has been translated

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting answer is exactly 500 languages, but the page says 'over 500 languages', so 500 is not the stated figure.

questions.question: Under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights page, which stages of education must be free, and which stage must be compulsory? Answer using the exact stages named in the passage.

sources.passage: Everyone has the right to education. Education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages. Elementary education shall be compulsory.

key.item: stages of education that shall be free
key.answer: at least in the elementary and fundamental stages

key.item: stage of education that shall be compulsory

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer that all education is free or compulsory. The passage limits free education to 'at least in the elementary and fundamental stages' and makes only 'Elementary education' compulsory.

questions.question: In the UNFCCC Convention text, how many days after the date of deposit of the fiftieth instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession does the Convention enter into force?

sources.passage: 1. The Convention shall enter into force on the ninetieth day after the date of deposit of the fiftieth instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession.

key.item: entry-into-force period after deposit of the fiftieth instrument

questions.commonly_confused: Thirty days is the Paris Agreement interval. The UNFCCC Convention text instead says the ninetieth day after deposit of the fiftieth instrument.

questions.question: Under the Kyoto Protocol text, by what year must each Party included in Annex I have made demonstrable progress in achieving its commitments under the Protocol?

sources.passage: Each Party included in Annex I shall, by  2005, have made demonstrable progress in achieving its commitments under this Protocol.

key.item: deadline year for demonstrable progress by Annex I Parties

questions.commonly_confused: People often quote 2008 to 2012 because that is the commitment period in another passage. The demonstrable-progress deadline in this passage is 2005.

questions.question: Using only the Paris Agreement publication page, how many days elapsed from the date the agreement was opened for signature to the date it entered into force? Count calendar days from 22 April 2016 to 4 November 2016.

sources.passage: The agreement was opened for signature on 22 April 2016 in New York. On 5 October 2016, the threshold for entry into force was achieved and the Paris Agreement entered into force on 4 November 2016.

key.item: calendar days from opening for signature to entry into force

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting answer is 30 days because the page also says entry into force is thirty days after the threshold is met. The question asks for the elapsed calendar days from 22 April 2016 to 4 November 2016, which is 196 days.

difficulty: newer instrument changed the quoted value
questions.question: A compliance note about the Paris Agreement still quotes the UNFCCC Convention's entry-into-force threshold of the fiftieth instrument and the ninetieth day. Using the Paris Agreement publication as in force on 2026-11-21, what Party-count and emissions-share thresholds, and what entry-into-force interval, should the note use for the Paris Agreement instead?

sources.passage: 1. The Convention shall enter into force on the ninetieth day after the date of deposit of the fiftieth instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession.

The Paris Agreement stipulates that it shall enter into force thirty days after the date on which at least 55 Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) accounting in total for at least an estimated 55 % of the total global greenhouse gas emissions have deposited their instruments of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession with the Depositary, the Secretary-General of the United Nations.

key.answer: at least 55 Parties to the UNFCCC
at least an estimated 55 % of the total global greenhouse gas emissions

questions.commonly_confused: The fiftieth instrument and ninetieth day belong to the UNFCCC Convention. The Paris Agreement is a separate, newer instrument with thresholds of at least 55 Parties and at least an estimated 55 % of total global greenhouse gas emissions, followed by a thirty-day interval.

questions.question: For the Convention on Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space, what is the difference in years between the year it was opened for signature and the year it entered into force? Use the dates in the UNOOSA publication and give the difference in calendar years.

key.item: difference in calendar years between opened for signature and entered into force

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer 2 years by subtracting 1974, the adoption year, from 1976. The question asks for the opened-for-signature year, 1975, and the entry-into-force year, 1976, so the difference is 1 year.

questions.question: Under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, if a coastal State uses the maximum breadth allowed for the territorial sea and the maximum contiguous-zone limit from the same baselines, how much farther from those baselines can the contiguous zone extend than the territorial sea? Give the answer in nautical miles.

sources.passage: Every State has the right to establish the breadth of its territorial sea up to a limit not exceeding 12 nautical miles, measured from baselines determined in accordance with this Convention.
The contiguous zone may not extend beyond 24 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of the territorial sea is measured.

key.item: difference between maximum contiguous-zone limit and maximum territorial-sea breadth

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting answer is 24 nautical miles, which is the outer contiguous-zone limit from the baselines. The question asks how much farther that is than the 12 nautical mile territorial sea, so the calculation is 24 minus 12, or 12 nautical miles.

questions.question: A reviewer says that, under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, a bay with natural entrance points 30 nautical miles apart may have a closing line drawn between those low-water marks, making the enclosed waters internal waters. Is that rule available under the passage? State the maximum entrance-point distance for that rule.

sources.passage: If the distance between the low-water marks of the natural entrance points of a bay does not exceed 24 nautical miles, a closing line may be drawn between these two low-water marks, and the waters enclosed thereby shall be considered as internal waters.

key.item: whether the closing-line rule applies to a 30 nautical mile bay entrance
maximum entrance-point distance for the closing-line rule

questions.commonly_confused: A reader might apply the internal-waters rule to any bay. The passage conditions it on the distance between low-water marks of natural entrance points not exceeding 24 nautical miles, so 30 nautical miles is outside that stated rule.

questions.question: On the supplied public text for the space-liability convention, an auditor wants a monetary cap on compensation for damage caused by a space object on the surface of the earth or to aircraft in flight. Does the passage stating absolute liability give such a monetary cap? If not, state what the passage does say about liability.

sources.passage:
Article H. A launching State shall be absolutely liable to pay compensation 
for damage caused by its space object on the surface of the earth or to aircraft in 
flight.

key.item: monetary cap in the absolute-liability passage
what the passage says about liability
key.answer: A launching State shall be absolutely liable to pay compensation for damage caused by its space object on the surface of the earth or to aircraft in flight

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may invent a damages ceiling because liability conventions often contain caps. The supplied passage states absolute liability to pay compensation but gives no monetary amount or cap.

difficulty: question names no rule or document
questions.question: A treaty file says that a party must give notice before denouncing or withdrawing from a treaty, but the file does not name the convention or article. In the supplied UN treaty text, what is the minimum notice period for a party's intention to denounce or withdraw from a treaty under paragraph 1?

sources.passage:
2. A party shall give not less than twelve months' notice of its intention to de 
nounce or withdraw from a treaty under paragraph 1.

key.item: minimum notice period for intention to denounce or withdraw

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting answer is twelve months after notification takes effect, but the passage is about giving notice of intention and says 'not less than twelve months' notice'.

questions.question: In the Optional Protocol to the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations concerning the compulsory jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice, what is the sum, in months, of the stated two-month period for agreeing to adopt a conciliation procedure and the stated five-month period after the conciliation commission's appointment for it to make its recommendations? Add only those two stated periods; do not treat the result as a deadline measured from notification of the dispute.

sources.passage: 1. Within the same period of two months, the parties may agree to adopt a conciliation procedure before resorting to the International Court of Justice.

2. The conciliation commission shall make its recommendations within five months after its appointment. If its recommendations are not accepted by the parties to the dispute within two months after they have been delivered, either party may bring the dispute before the Court by an application.

key.item: sum of the two-month conciliation-agreement period and the five-month post-appointment recommendation period

questions.commonly_confused: Five months uses only the recommendation period, while nine months wrongly adds the later two-month period for accepting the recommendations. The requested arithmetic is 2 + 5 = 7 months; it is not a maximum elapsed time from dispute notification because the supplied text does not establish when the commission is appointed.

difficulty: newer edition or addendum changed the quoted value
questions.question: A compliance file still cites the WHO publication page's 'fourth edition' wording for Guidelines for drinking-water quality. In the supplied WHO publication page text, what updated version does the page tell readers to access, and what does the page say the first addendum does?

sources.passage: This first addendum updates the fourth edition. Updates reflect new evidence and further, provides additional explanations to support better understanding and application of the guidance.
Access here the latest and updated version of this publication: Guidelines for drinking-water quality - Fourth edition incorporating the first and second addenda

key.item: updated version the page tells readers to access
key.answer: Guidelines for drinking-water quality - Fourth edition incorporating the first and second addenda
It updates the fourth edition; the updates reflect new evidence and provide additional explanations to support better understanding and application of the guidance.

questions.commonly_confused: The tempting answer is simply 'the fourth edition' or 'the fourth edition incorporating the first addendum'. The supplied text instead directs readers to the fourth edition incorporating the first and second addenda and separately explains that the first addendum updates the fourth edition.

questions.question: In RFC 7519, what is the exact rule for a JWT Claims Set that has duplicate Claim Names?

sources.passage: The Claim Names within a JWT Claims Set MUST be unique; JWT parsers MUST either reject JWTs with duplicate Claim Names or use a JSON parser that returns only the lexically last duplicate member name, as specified in Section 15.12 ("The JSON Object") of ECMAScript 5.1 [ECMAScript].

key.answer: Claim Names MUST be unique; parsers MUST either reject the JWT or use a JSON parser that returns only the lexically last duplicate member name

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting answer is that parsers may simply accept the first duplicate or any duplicate. RFC 7519 instead requires rejection or the lexically last duplicate member name.

questions.question: In RFC 7519, of the signature and MAC algorithms specified in JSON Web Algorithms, which ones MUST be implemented by conforming JWT implementations?

sources.passage: Of the signature and MAC algorithms specified in JSON Web Algorithms [JWA], only HMAC SHA-256 ("HS256") and "none" MUST be implemented by conforming JWT implementations.

questions.commonly_confused: People often quote RS256 as mandatory because it is widely used, but RFC 7519 says only HS256 and none MUST be implemented.

questions.question: In RFC 7515, how many signatures or MACs are supported by the JWS Compact Serialization, and what header syntax does it lack?

sources.passage: Only one signature/MAC is supported by the JWS Compact Serialization and it provides no syntax to represent a JWS Unprotected Header value.

key.answer: no syntax to represent a JWS Unprotected Header value

questions.commonly_confused: The JWS JSON Serialization can represent multiple signatures, so a reader may wrongly carry that over to compact serialization. RFC 7515 limits compact serialization to one signature/MAC and no unprotected header syntax.

questions.question: An auditor asks: under RFC 6749, what mandatory rules does OAuth 2.0 set for the interaction between the authorization server and the resource server? Give the rule, or say if the RFC states none.

sources.passage: The interaction between the authorization server and resource server is beyond the scope of this specification.  The authorization server may be the same server as the resource server or a separate entity.  A single authorization server may issue access tokens accepted by multiple resource servers.

key.answer: none; the interaction is beyond the scope of RFC 6749

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is to invent token-validation or introspection requirements. The passage says the interaction is beyond scope; the following sentences only describe possible arrangements, not mandatory rules.

questions.question: In RFC 6750, if a client uses the form-encoded body parameter method to send a bearer access token, which HTTP request method is specifically forbidden?

sources.passage: The HTTP request method is one for which the request-body has defined semantics. In particular, this means that the "GET" method MUST NOT be used.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer POST because the passage requires defined request-body semantics, but the RFC explicitly says GET MUST NOT be used.

questions.question: RFC 7636 recommends a 32-octet random sequence that is base64url-encoded into a 43-octet code verifier, and separately says the client SHOULD create a code_verifier with a minimum of 256 bits of entropy. Using only those stated numbers, how many bits of entropy are in the 32-octet sequence?

sources.passage: It is RECOMMENDED that the output of a suitable random number generator be used to create a 32-octet sequence.  The octet sequence is then base64url-encoded to produce a 43-octet URL safe string to use as the code verifier.
The client SHOULD create a "code_verifier" with a minimum of 256 bits of entropy.  This can be done by having a suitable random number generator create a 32-octet sequence.

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is 43 bytes or 344 bits, from the encoded verifier length. The entropy comes from the 32-octet random sequence: 32 × 8 = 256 bits, which the second passage also states.

difficulty: newer edition, amendment or corrigendum changed the value
questions.question: In RFC 7636, what is the default value of code_challenge_method when it is absent, and what is the rule for a client that is capable of using S256?

sources.passage:
code_challenge_method
      OPTIONAL, defaults to "plain" if not present in the request.  Code
      verifier transformation method is "S256" or "plain".

If the client is capable of using "S256", it MUST use "S256", as "S256" is Mandatory To Implement (MTI) on the server.  Clients are permitted to use "plain" only if they cannot support "S256" for some technical reason and know via out-of-band configuration that the server supports "plain".

key.item: rule for client capable of S256

questions.commonly_confused: People often quote S256 as the default because it is mandatory to implement and required for capable clients. RFC 7636 still says the omitted parameter defaults to plain.

questions.question: RFC 8446 says the basic data block size is one byte, and that TLSPlaintext records carry data in chunks of 2^14 bytes or less. What is the maximum TLSPlaintext record data chunk in bytes, in decimal?

sources.passage: The basic data block size is one byte (i.e., 8 bits).  Multiple-byte data items are concatenations of bytes, from left to right, from top to bottom.
The record layer fragments information blocks into TLSPlaintext records carrying data in chunks of 2^14 bytes or less.

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is 2^14 bits or 2048 bytes. The passage says bytes, and 2^14 bytes is 16,384 bytes.

difficulty: newer edition, amendment or corrigendum changed the value
questions.question: In RFC 5280, what is the maximum email address length after the change from RFC 3280, and what was the old value? Also, through which year must conforming CAs encode certificate validity dates as UTCTime?

sources.passage: The ASN.1 modules in Appendix A are unchanged from RFC 3280, except that ub-emailaddress-length was changed from 128 to 255 in order to align with PKCS #9 [RFC2985].
CAs conforming to this profile MUST always encode certificate validity dates through the year 2049 as UTCTime; certificate validity dates in 2050 or later MUST be encoded as GeneralizedTime.

key.item: maximum email address length after change
last year for UTCTime validity dates

questions.commonly_confused: The old 128 value is still quoted from RFC 3280, but RFC 5280 says it was changed to 255. A separate tempting error is to use 2050 as the UTCTime cutoff; RFC 5280 says through 2049 is UTCTime and 2050 or later is GeneralizedTime.

questions.question: In RFC 6960, when a responder sends a revoked response for a non-issued certificate, what revocation reason and revocationTime MUST the related SingleResponse specify?

sources.passage: When a responder sends a "revoked" response to a status request for a non-issued certificate, the responder MUST include the extended revoked definition response extension (Section 4.4.8) in the response, indicating that the OCSP responder supports the extended definition of the "revoked" state to also cover non-issued certificates. In addition, the SingleResponse related to this non-issued certificate:

- MUST specify the revocation reason certificateHold (6),

   - MUST specify the revocationTime January 1, 1970, and

   - MUST NOT include a CRL references extension (Section 4.4.2) or any
     CRL entry extensions (Section 4.4.5).

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is to treat a non-issued certificate as unknown or good. RFC 6960 has a special extended revoked definition requiring certificateHold (6) and January 1, 1970.

questions.question: In RFC 8657, what DNS resolver requirement applies to a CA that supports the CAA accounturi parameter or the validationmethods parameter?

sources.passage: A CA supporting the "accounturi" parameter or the "validationmethods" parameter MUST perform CAA validation using a trusted DNSSEC-validating resolver.

key.answer: MUST perform CAA validation using a trusted DNSSEC-validating resolver

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is ordinary DNS validation, or DNSSEC only when accounturi is used. The passage applies to either parameter and requires a trusted DNSSEC-validating resolver.

difficulty: question names no rule or document
questions.question: For a public web vulnerability-reporting file placed at the well-known security.txt location, what HTTP version, scheme, and Content-Type with default charset does the file format specification require?

sources.passage: The file MUST be accessed via HTTP 1.0 or a higher version, and the file access MUST use the "https" scheme (as per Section 2.7.2 of [RFC7230]).  It MUST have a Content-Type of "text/plain" with the default charset parameter set to "utf-8" (as per Section 4.1.3 of [RFC2046]).

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is plain HTTP because the file is public, or text/html because it is served on the web (or application/json because the format is machine-parsable); the cited rule requires https and text/plain with default charset utf-8.

questions.question: In Content Security Policy Level 3, if frame-ancestors is placed in a policy declared via a meta element, what framing restrictions does that directive impose? Give the rule, or say if the directive has no effect.

sources.passage: The frame-ancestors directive MUST be ignored when contained in a policy declared via a meta element.
Note: The Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header is not supported inside a meta element. Neither are the report-uri, frame-ancestors, and sandbox directives.

key.item: framing restrictions imposed by frame-ancestors in a meta-element policy
key.answer: none; the directive MUST be ignored

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is to apply the listed ancestors as a framing allowlist. CSP3 says frame-ancestors is not supported in a meta element and MUST be ignored there.

questions.question: RFC 9106 says Argon2id MUST be supported and gives its first recommended option as t=1 with 2 GiB memory. It also says the internal compression function G has two 1024-byte inputs. How many bytes of input does one call to G take in total?

sources.passage: Argon2id MUST be supported by any implementation of this document, whereas Argon2d and Argon2i MAY be supported.

The Argon2id variant with t=1 and 2 GiB memory is the FIRST
   RECOMMENDED option and is suggested as a default setting for all
   environments.

Argon2 uses an internal compression function G with two 1024-byte
   inputs, a 1024-byte output, and an internal hash function H^x(), with
   x being its output length in bytes.

key.item: total input bytes for one call to G

questions.commonly_confused: A tempting wrong answer is 1024 bytes, taking one of the two inputs as the whole input, or 2 GiB, confusing the recommended memory setting with G's input size. The calculation is 2 × 1024 = 2048 bytes.

questions.question: In RFC 8259, what exact encoding is required for JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem?

sources.passage: JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8 [RFC3629].

questions.commonly_confused: UTF-16 or UTF-8 with a byte order mark are tempting because other text formats allow them, but RFC 8259 requires UTF-8 here and separately says implementations MUST NOT add a byte order mark to networked-transmitted JSON text.

questions.question: RFC 8259 says integer JSON numbers in what inclusive range are interoperable when software of the kind described is used? Give the range using the same 2**53 notation as the RFC.

sources.passage: Note that when such software is used, numbers that are integers and are in the range [-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1] are interoperable in the sense that implementations will agree exactly on their numeric values.

questions.commonly_confused: People often quote [-(2**53), (2**53)] or the ECMAScript safe-integer range [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991] in decimal; the RFC passage gives the endpoints in 2**53 notation.

questions.question: In XML 1.0 Fifth Edition, which two Unicode encodings must all XML processors accept?

sources.passage:
All XML processors MUST accept the UTF-8 and UTF-16
encodings of Unicode [Unicode];
the mechanisms for signaling which of the two is in use,
or for bringing other encodings into play, are discussed later, in 4.3.3 Character Encoding in Entities.

key.item: encodings all XML processors must accept

questions.commonly_confused: UTF-32 or ISO-8859-1 may be assumed from general Unicode or web practice, but the XML 1.0 Fifth Edition passage names only UTF-8 and UTF-16 as mandatory for all processors.

questions.question: Using the WOFF2 File Format 2.0 description, what is the total byte length of the fixed-size parts of a complete WOFF2 file with no collection, no extended metadata, no private data, and no padding, if the WAL-like header detail is ignored? Use the WOFF2 header size from the file-format description and the WAL header size from the SQLite page only as a cross-check of header sizes; report the WOFF2 value.

sources.passage: A complete WOFF2 file consists of several blocks of data: a 48-byte header, immediately followed (in this order) by a variable-size Table Directory, an optional Collection Directory (present only if the input font file is a font collection), a compressed font data block, an optional block of Extended Metadata, and an optional block of Private Data.
The WAL header is 32 bytes in size and consists of the following eight big-endian 32-bit unsigned integer values:

key.item: fixed-size parts total for the stated WOFF2 file

questions.commonly_confused: 32 bytes is tempting because the SQLite WAL header is 32 bytes, but that is a different format; the WOFF2 description says its header is 48 bytes and the other listed blocks are variable-size or optional.

questions.question: In WOFF2 File Format 2.0, what exact signature field value must a WOFF2 header contain, and what must user agents do if it does not contain that value?

sources.passage: The signature field in the WOFF2 header MUST contain the value of 0x774F4632 ('wOF2'), which distinguishes it from WOFF 1.0 files. If the field does not contain this value, user agents MUST reject the file as invalid.

key.item: required user-agent action if signature is wrong

questions.commonly_confused: The WOFF 1.0 signature 'wOFF' is tempting because WOFF2 is a newer version, but the passage says 0x774F4632 ('wOF2') distinguishes it from WOFF 1.0 files.

questions.question: In ECMA-262 15th Edition (ECMAScript 2024), what is the maximum length of a String value? Answer in elements, using ASCII exponent notation for the value whose exponent is printed as a superscript in the specification.

sources.passage: The String type is the set of all ordered sequences of zero or more 16-bit unsigned integer values (“elements”) up to a maximum length of 253 - 1 elements.

questions.commonly_confused: Answering in bytes or giving 2^53 elements would misstate the passage. It defines the elements as 16-bit unsigned integer values and sets the maximum length at 2^53 - 1 elements.

difficulty: newer edition or amendment changed the value
questions.question: In The Go Programming Language Specification, which Go version is attached to the built-in clear function, and which Go version is attached to the built-in min and max functions?

sources.passage:
The built-in function clear takes an argument of map,
slice, or type parameter type,
and deletes or zeroes out all elements
[Go 1.21].

The built-in functions min and max compute the
smallest—or largest, respectively—value of a fixed number of
arguments of ordered types.
There must be at least one argument
[Go 1.21].

key.item: Go version attached to min and max

questions.commonly_confused: Go 1.18 is tempting because generics arrived then, but the passages for clear and for min/max are both marked [Go 1.21].

questions.question: For a SQLite database file using the smallest allowed page size, what is the largest reserved-space byte count allowed by the usable-size rule? Use the page-size limit and the usable-size rule from the SQLite Database File Format document.

sources.passage: The size of a page is a power of two between 512 and 65536 inclusive.  All pages within the same database are the same size.  The page size for a database file is determined by the 2-byte integer located at an offset of 16 bytes from the beginning of the database file.
However, the usable size is not allowed to be less than 480.  In other words, if the page size is 512, then the reserved space size cannot exceed 32.

key.item: largest reserved-space byte count at that page size

questions.commonly_confused: 480 bytes is the minimum usable size, not the reserved-space allowance; at a 512-byte page, 512 - 480 = 32 bytes, and the passage states that value directly.

questions.question: An engineer asks for the IANA-assigned service name for a TCP port in the Dynamic and/or Private Ports range of the IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry, as in force on 2026-11-21. What is the defensible answer from the registry scope rule?

sources.passage: Dynamic and/or Private Ports (49152-65535) are not assigned.

key.item: IANA-assigned service name for a TCP port in the Dynamic and/or Private Ports range
key.answer: none; Dynamic and/or Private Ports (49152-65535) are not assigned

questions.commonly_confused: A vendor-specific service name may be found in local configuration or folklore, but the registry rule says ports 49152-65535 are not assigned, so there is no IANA-assigned service name to report.

questions.question: A compliance reviewer asks which subtype under the IANA 'example' media type is registered for a new documentation example, as in force on 2026-11-21. What does the IANA Media Types Registry rule say?

sources.passage:
The 'example' media type is used for examples. Any subtype following the media
type syntax may be used in those examples. No subtype can be registered with
IANA.

key.item: registered subtype under the 'example' media type
key.answer: none; no subtype can be registered with IANA

questions.commonly_confused: Names such as example/foo are tempting because the registry says any syntactically valid subtype may be used in examples, but that same rule says no subtype can be registered with IANA.

difficulty: newer edition or amendment changed the value
questions.question: RFC 5280 says one ASN.1 upper bound was changed from an older RFC 3280 value to a new value to align with PKCS #9. What is the name of that bound, and what are the old and new values?

sources.passage: The ASN.1 modules in Appendix A are unchanged from RFC 3280, except that ub-emailaddress-length was changed from 128 to 255 in order to align with PKCS #9 [RFC2985].

questions.commonly_confused: 128 is still quoted from RFC 3280, but RFC 5280 explicitly says ub-emailaddress-length was changed from 128 to 255.

difficulty: question names no rule or document
questions.question: A service sends JSON over the public internet. The payload uses uppercase TRUE and the sender adds U+FEFF at the start of the transmitted text. Which public specification should be checked, and what two rules does it state about these literal names and the byte order mark?

sources.passage: The literal names MUST be lowercase.  No other literal names are allowed.
Implementations MUST NOT add a byte order mark (U+FEFF) to the beginning of a networked-transmitted JSON text.
JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8 [RFC3629].

key.answer: RFC 8259: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format
literal names MUST be lowercase; no other literal names are allowed
implementations MUST NOT add a byte order mark (U+FEFF) to the beginning of a networked-transmitted JSON text

questions.commonly_confused: ECMA-404 is tempting because it is also a JSON syntax specification, but the supplied ECMA-404 passages define syntax scope and do not state these two network JSON rules; RFC 8259 states both.

questions.question: In SPARQL 1.1 Query Language, what does the LIMIT clause put an upper bound on?

sources.passage: The LIMIT clause puts an upper bound on the number of solutions returned.

questions.commonly_confused: SQL-style row counts or query execution time are tempting, but the SPARQL passage says the upper bound is on the number of solutions returned.

questions.question: In RFC 8259, how many primitive types and how many structured types can JSON represent?

sources.passage: JSON can represent four primitive types (strings, numbers, booleans, and null) and two structured types (objects and arrays).

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may count the six named categories as one flat list and answer only 6. The passage separates them into four primitive types and two structured types.

questions.question: In RFC 3629, what is the maximum number of octets in a UTF-8 sequence for characters in the U+0000..U+10FFFF range?

sources.passage:
In UTF-8, characters from the U+0000..U+10FFFF range (the UTF-16
   accessible range) are encoded using sequences of 1 to 4 octets.

questions.commonly_confused: Older or informal descriptions of UTF-8 may mention 5 or 6 octets. RFC 3629 limits the stated range to sequences of 1 to 4 octets.

questions.question: RFC 4648 says MIME enforces a limit on line length of base 64-encoded data. What is that MIME line-length limit, in characters?

sources.passage: As such, MIME enforces a limit on line length of base 64-encoded data to 76 characters.  MIME inherits the encoding from Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) [3], stating that it is "virtually identical"; however, PEM uses a line length of 64 characters.

questions.commonly_confused: 64 characters is the PEM line length in the same passage, not the MIME limit asked for.

questions.question: In RFC 3339, what hour values does this profile of ISO 8601 allow?

sources.passage:
Although ISO 8601 permits the hour to be "24", this profile of ISO
   8601 only allows values between "00" and "23" for the hour in order
   to reduce confusion.

questions.commonly_confused: ISO 8601 permits hour "24", but the RFC 3339 profile does not; a careful reader answers with the profile's allowed range.

questions.question: In RFC 6902, list the values allowed for an operation object's "op" member.

sources.passage:
Operation objects MUST have exactly one "op" member, whose value
   indicates the operation to perform.  Its value MUST be one of "add",
   "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", or "test"; other values are
   errors.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may add plausible patch verbs such as "merge" or "append". The passage says other values are errors.

questions.question: Using RFC 4648, how many encoded characters are produced from 9 octets of input by the base64 encoding process, and what default rule applies to pad characters at the end of encoded data?

sources.passage: The encoding process represents 24-bit groups of input bits as output strings of 4 encoded characters.  Proceeding from left to right, a 24-bit input group is formed by concatenating 3 8-bit input groups.
Implementations MUST include appropriate pad characters at the end of encoded data unless the specification referring to this document explicitly states otherwise.

key.answer: Implementations MUST include appropriate pad characters at the end of encoded data unless the specification referring to this document explicitly states otherwise.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer 36 characters by treating each of the 9 octets as a 24-bit group that produces 4 characters. The passage says 3 octets make one 24-bit group and produce 4 characters; 9 octets make 3 groups, so 3 × 4 = 12. Another mistake is to omit padding because some profiles do; RFC 4648 makes padding the default.

questions.question: For RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme, what encoding must the final result use, and how must U+000B be serialized under the ASCII control-character rule?

sources.passage:
Finally, in order to create a platform-independent representation,
   the result of the preceding step MUST be encoded in UTF-8.

If the Unicode value falls within the traditional ASCII control
      character range (U+0000 through U+001F), it MUST be serialized
      using lowercase hexadecimal Unicode notation (\uhhhh) unless it is
      in the set of predefined JSON control characters U+0008, U+0009,
      U+000A, U+000C, or U+000D, which MUST be serialized as \b, \t, \n,
      \f, and \r, respectively.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may use \v or a short escape for vertical tab, or uppercase \u000B. The passage gives short escapes only for five listed control characters and requires lowercase hexadecimal Unicode notation otherwise.

questions.question: In XML 1.0 Fifth Edition, which Unicode encodings must all XML processors accept?

sources.passage: All XML processors MUST accept the UTF-8 and UTF-16 encodings of Unicode [Unicode];

key.item: encodings all XML processors must accept

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer only UTF-8 because it is the common XML encoding. The passage requires both UTF-8 and UTF-16.

questions.question: In W3C XML Schema Definition Language 1.1 Part 2, the value space of float uses m × 2^e with |m| less than 2^24, and double uses |m| less than 2^53. How many times larger is the double mantissa bound than the float mantissa bound?

sources.passage: The ·value space· of float contains the non-zero numbers m × 2e , where m is an integer whose absolute value is less than 224, and e is an integer between −149 and 104, inclusive.
The ·value space· of double contains the non-zero numbers m × 2e , where m is an integer whose absolute value is less than 253, and e is an integer between −1074 and 971, inclusive.

key.item: ratio of double mantissa bound to float mantissa bound

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer 29 times by subtracting the exponents, or 2^53 / 2^24 as 2^29 but forget to give the numeric value. The calculation is 2^53 / 2^24 = 2^29 = 536,870,912.

questions.question: In CSS Values and Units Module Level 4, what is the minimum number of repetitions of a repeated component value that user agents must support, and what is the minimum number of calc-value terms they must support in calculations?

sources.passage:
For repeated component values (indicated by *, +, or #), UAs must support at least 20 repetitions of the component.
	If a property value contains more than the supported number of repetitions,
	the declaration must be ignored as if it were invalid.

UAs must support calculations of at least 32 <calc-value> terms
	and at least 32 levels of nesting (parentheses and/or functions).
	For functions that support an arbitrary number of arguments (such as min()),
	it must also support at least 32 arguments.

questions.commonly_confused: Both nearby limits include 32, so a reader may answer 32 repetitions. The repetition limit is 20; 32 applies to calc-value terms, nesting levels, and arbitrary arguments.

questions.question: For the 06 October 2026 Candidate Recommendation Snapshot of SVG 2, what is the earliest date on which this Candidate Recommendation is expected to advance to Recommendation?

sources.passage: This document is the 06 October 2026 Candidate Recommendation Snapshot of SVG 2.  This version of SVG builds upon SVG 1.1 Second Edition by improving the usability of the language and by adding new features commonly requested by authors.
This Candidate Recommendation is expected to advance to Recommendation no earlier than 01 December 2026.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may quote 06 October 2026, the snapshot date, or assume SVG 2 is already a Recommendation because SVG 1.1 Second Edition is older. The passage gives a later no-earlier-than date for advancement.

questions.question: A compliance reviewer asks: under UI Events, what mouse wheel event type must a user agent dispatch when a document wheel is used? What does the specification say about that section?

sources.passage: The Mouse Events and Wheel Events section of this specification have been moved to the Pointer Events specification [pointerevents4].

key.item: mouse wheel event type in UI Events
key.answer: No such value is stated in UI Events; the Mouse Events and Wheel Events section has been moved to the Pointer Events specification [pointerevents4].

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may answer "wheel" or a legacy mouse wheel event name from memory. The cited scope passage says that section has been moved, so UI Events does not supply the requested event type.

questions.question: In Resource Timing Level 2, will an HTML IMG element whose source is a data: URI be included as a PerformanceResourceTiming object in the Performance Timeline?

sources.passage: If an HTML IMG element has a data: URI as its source [RFC2397], then this resource will not be included as a PerformanceResourceTiming object in the Performance Timeline. PerformanceResourceTiming entries are only reported for http(s) resources.

key.item: inclusion of HTML IMG with data: URI
key.answer: No; it will not be included. PerformanceResourceTiming entries are only reported for http(s) resources.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may apply the general rule that resources fetched by a non-null client are included, or that HTTP-cache resources are included. The specific scope passage excludes data: URI images and says entries are only reported for http(s) resources.

questions.question: A web-performance engineer asks: for a browser timing API, what time resolution must be used when crossOriginIsolatedCapability is false, and what time resolution must be used when crossOriginIsolatedCapability is true? Find the public specification that states these limits.

sources.passage:
Let time resolution be 100 microseconds, or a higher
    implementation-defined value.
    
    
     If crossOriginIsolatedCapability is true, set time resolution
    to be 5 microseconds, or a higher implementation-defined
    value.

key.item: time resolution when crossOriginIsolatedCapability is false
key.answer: 100 microseconds, or a higher implementation-defined value

key.item: time resolution when crossOriginIsolatedCapability is true
key.answer: 5 microseconds, or a higher implementation-defined value

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may give only 5 microseconds because the isolated case is explicitly named, or may give 0.2 microseconds from the DOMHighResTimeStamp finite-resolution note. The passage first sets the default to 100 microseconds and then changes it to 5 microseconds only when crossOriginIsolatedCapability is true.

questions.question: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, as in force on 2026-11-21, what is the employer's general duty to employees, and what qualification limits that duty?

sources.passage: (1)It shall be the duty of every employer to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare at work of all his employees.

key.answer: to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare at work of all his employees

questions.commonly_confused: An absolute duty to ensure health, safety and welfare; the passage qualifies the duty with 'so far as is reasonably practicable'.

questions.question: Under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, as in force on 2026-11-21, what written statement must every employer prepare and revise, subject to prescribed exceptions, and to whom must the statement and any revision be brought?

sources.passage: (3)Except in such cases as may be prescribed, it shall be the duty of every employer to prepare and as often as may be appropriate revise a written statement of his general policy with respect to the health and safety at work of his employees and the organisation and arrangements for the time being in force for carrying out that policy, and to bring the statement and any revision of it to the notice of all of his employees.

key.answer: a written statement of the employer's general policy with respect to the health and safety at work of employees and the organisation and arrangements for carrying out that policy

questions.commonly_confused: That only a risk assessment must be prepared; the passage requires a written statement of general policy, organisation and arrangements, and notice to all employees.

questions.field: UK health and safety arrangements recording threshold
questions.question: For the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, in the latest available (Revised) version shown on the supplied page, give the coming-into-force date and the employee-count threshold at which the employer must record the health and safety arrangements referred to in regulation 5(1).

sources.passage: These Regulations may be cited as the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 and shall come into force on 29th December 1999.
Where the employer employs five or more employees, he shall record the arrangements referred to in paragraph (1).

key.item: employee-count threshold for recording the arrangements referred to in regulation 5(1)

questions.commonly_confused: The threshold is sometimes misquoted as 'more than 5 employees'; the passage says 'five or more employees'. It is also a trap to call these 'risk-assessment arrangements': the cited passage is about the arrangements referred to in paragraph (1) of regulation 5.

questions.question: A compliance file asks whether, under the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 as in force on 2026-11-21, the Regulations apply to the master or crew of a ship, or their employer, for normal ship-board activities carried out solely by the crew under the master's direction. What is the answer from the scope clause?

sources.passage: These Regulations shall not apply to or in relation to the master or crew of a ship, or to the employer of such persons, in respect of the normal ship-board activities of a ship’s crew which are carried out solely by the crew under the direction of the master.

key.item: application to master or crew and employer for those activities
key.answer: No; the Regulations shall not apply to or in relation to them in respect of those normal ship-board activities

questions.commonly_confused: That the Regulations apply because they are UK workplace safety regulations; the scope clause expressly excludes this ship-crew case.

questions.field: UK power press thorough examination intervals
questions.question: Under the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998, in the latest available (Revised) version shown on the supplied page, how often must a power press with fixed guards only be thoroughly examined, and how often in other cases? Also state the additional event that requires thorough examination.

sources.passage: (i)at least every 12 months, where it has fixed guards only; or (ii)at least every 6 months, in other cases; and (iii)each time that exceptional circumstances have occurred which are liable to jeopardise the safety of the power press or its guards or protection devices; and

key.item: fixed guards only thorough examination interval

key.answer: each time that exceptional circumstances have occurred which are liable to jeopardise the safety of the power press or its guards or protection devices

questions.commonly_confused: Reversing the 12-month and 6-month intervals; the passage gives 12 months only for fixed guards and 6 months in other cases. It is also wrong to call this the separate PUWER 'inspection' duty; the question asks for the thorough examination intervals.

questions.question: A distributor supplies work equipment by way of sale and asks whether the requirements of the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998, as in force on 2026-11-21, apply to that person in respect of equipment supplied by sale. What does the scope clause say?

sources.passage: (5) The requirements imposed by these Regulations shall not apply to a person in respect of work equipment supplied by him by way of sale, agreement for sale or hire-purchase agreement.

key.item: application of PUWER requirements to person supplying equipment by sale
key.answer: No; the requirements shall not apply to a person in respect of work equipment supplied by him by way of sale, agreement for sale or hire-purchase agreement

questions.commonly_confused: That PUWER always applies to any supplier of work equipment; the scope clause excludes a person in respect of equipment supplied by sale, agreement for sale or hire-purchase agreement.

questions.question: Under the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002, as in force on 2026-11-21, for how long must a suitable record of examinations and tests of local exhaust ventilation plant, and repairs carried out as a result, or a suitable summary, be kept available?

sources.passage: Every employer shall keep a suitable record of the examinations and tests carried out in accordance with paragraphs (2) and (3) and of repairs carried out as a result of those examinations and tests, and that record or a suitable summary thereof shall be kept available for at least 5 years from the date on which it was made.

key.answer: at least 5 years from the date on which it was made

questions.commonly_confused: Three years, by confusing this with RIDDOR record keeping; the COSHH passage says at least 5 years.

questions.question: Under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations 2013, as in force on 2026-11-21, when a person at work is incapacitated for routine work for more than seven consecutive days because of a work-accident injury, excluding the day of the accident, by when must the responsible person send the report?

sources.passage: (2) Where any person at work is incapacitated for routine work for more than seven consecutive days (excluding the day of the accident) because of an injury resulting from an accident arising out of or in connection with that work, the responsible person must send a report to the relevant enforcing authority in an approved manner as soon as practicable and in any event within 15 days of the accident.

key.answer: as soon as practicable and in any event within 15 days of the accident

questions.commonly_confused: Seven days from the accident; seven consecutive days is the incapacity trigger, while the report deadline is within 15 days of the accident.

questions.question: For U.S. standard-gauge railroad track subject to 49 CFR Part 213, as in force on 2026-11-21, where is gage measured between the rail heads, and how far below the top of the rail head is that measurement plane?

sources.passage: (a) Gage is measured between the heads of the rails at right-angles to the rails in a plane five-eighths of an inch below the top of the rail head.

key.answer: between the heads of the rails at right-angles to the rails

key.item: measurement plane below top of rail head

questions.commonly_confused: At the top of the rail head; the rule places the plane five-eighths of an inch below the top of the rail head.

questions.question: A track engineer asks whether, under 49 CFR Part 213 as in force on 2026-11-21, requirements specified for curved track apply to a curve of 0.20 degree, unless otherwise provided in the part. What is the answer from the scope clause?

sources.passage: Unless otherwise provided in this part, requirements specified for curved track apply only to track having a curvature greater than 0.25 degree.

key.item: application of curved-track requirements to 0.20 degree curve
key.answer: No; unless otherwise provided, they apply only to track having a curvature greater than 0.25 degree

questions.commonly_confused: That any curved track is covered; the scope clause sets a greater-than-0.25-degree threshold.

questions.question: Under 49 CFR Part 229 as in force on 2026-11-21, state the scope of the part regarding steam locomotives, and give the minimum and maximum sound level required for each lead locomotive's horn at 100 feet forward.

sources.passage: This part prescribes minimum Federal safety standards for all locomotives except those propelled by steam power.

Each lead locomotive shall be equipped with a locomotive horn that produces a minimum sound level of 96 dB(A) and a maximum sound level of 110 dB(A) at 100 feet forward of the locomotive in its direction of travel.

key.answer: the part prescribes minimum Federal safety standards for all locomotives except those propelled by steam power

questions.commonly_confused: Applying the horn rule to steam locomotives or quoting only 96 dB(A); the part excludes steam-powered locomotives and the horn passage gives both 96 dB(A) minimum and 110 dB(A) maximum.

questions.question: For 47 CFR Part 73 as in force on 2026-11-21, AM broadcast carrier frequencies begin at 540 kHz, progress in 10 kHz steps, and end at 1700 kHz. How many 10 kHz steps are there from 540 kHz to 1700 kHz, and how many carrier frequencies does the rule say are assigned?

sources.passage: The 117 carrier frequencies assigned to AM broadcast stations begin at 540 kHz and progress in 10 kHz steps to 1700 kHz.

key.item: number of 10 kHz steps from 540 kHz to 1700 kHz

questions.question: Under 47 CFR Part 95 as in force on 2026-11-21, FRS has 22 channels. For an FRS transmitter type, what ERP limit applies on channels 8 through 14, and what ERP limit applies on channels 1 through 7 and 15 through 22? Do not use the old blanket 2 W figure.

key.answer: flood with a 2-percent chance of being exceeded in any given year

total minimum freeboard in those locations

no higher than 1 foot above grade

Manning n with a plane bed

378.Donations not amounting to more than £5,000 in any twelve month period

586.Public companies: shares must be at least one-quarter paid up

questions.commonly_confused: Applying 10,000 words to every motion is tempting because that limit appears first. The second sentence imposes the lower 2,500-word limit on other motions.

questions.question: An online retailer is drafting withdrawal instructions under Directive 2011/83/EU, using the text at CELEX 32011L0083. When does the withdrawal period expire for a service contract and for a sales contract?

key.answer: After 14 days from conclusion of the contract.
After 14 days from the day on which the consumer, or a third party other than the carrier and indicated by the consumer, acquires physical possession of the goods.

questions.commonly_confused: Running both periods from conclusion of the contract is tempting because that is the service-contract rule. For sales contracts, the quoted passage instead uses acquisition of physical possession.

questions.question: A fair-trial training module needs the exact presumption stated by the European Convention on Human Rights, in the text presented as amended through Protocol No. 15. What presumption applies to everyone charged with a criminal offence?

Everyone charged with a criminal offence shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.

key.item: Presumption for a person charged with a criminal offence
key.answer: The person shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader might substitute a familiar formulation about proof beyond reasonable doubt. The quoted Convention rule is specifically a presumption of innocence until guilt is proved according to law.

questions.question: In a single-respondent FTC adjudication under 16 CFR Part 3 as in force on 2026-11-21, suppose the respondent uses the entire answer period and the Administrative Law Judge then uses the entire period allowed after that answer to hold the scheduling conference. sources.passage: A respondent shall file an answer within 14 days after being served with the complaint.
Not later than 10 days after the answer is filed by the last answering respondent, the Administrative Law Judge shall hold a scheduling conference.

questions.commonly_confused: Ten days after service of the complaint is tempting if the scheduling-conference sentence is read alone. The ten-day period starts after the answer, which itself may be filed up to 14 days after service.

First undertaking's margin above its Community-wide turnover threshold
Second undertaking's margin above its Community-wide turnover threshold

Whether the maximum-value optional exclusion covers the pair

questions.question: An old training slide says that judges of the European Court of Human Rights serve renewable six-year terms. In the Convention text presented as amended through Protocol No. 15, what is the election term, and may a judge be re-elected?

The judges shall be elected for a period of nine years. They may not be re-elected.

questions.commonly_confused: The renewable six-year term is tempting because it appears in older descriptions of the Court. The amended text instead states a nine-year term and expressly prohibits re-election.

questions.question: Can a State-aid team rely on Commission Regulation (EU) No 651/2014 to exempt aid to facilitate the closure of an uncompetitive coal mine from notification? If not, which instrument does the Regulation's scope passage identify as dealing with that aid?

key.answer: No; the Regulation should not apply to aid to facilitate the closure of uncompetitive coal mines.
The Council Decision of 10 December 2010 on State aid to facilitate the closure of uncompetitive coal mines.

questions.commonly_confused: Yes is tempting because the next sentence says that the Regulation should apply to other types of aid in the coal sector. That sentence does not override the express exclusion of mine-closure aid.

questions.question: A Contracting State invokes the European Convention on Human Rights' emergency derogation provision during a war. May it derogate from Article 3 under that provision, and what narrow Article 2 exception does the same non-derogation clause state?

Deaths resulting from lawful acts of war.

questions.commonly_confused: A reader may generalize the lawful-acts-of-war exception into permission for broad emergency derogations. The exception is attached to Article 2 only; Article 3 remains non-derogable under the quoted clause.

questions.commonly_confused: A text concerned only with recognition and enforcement is tempting because those words appear at the end of the description. The passage describes a model law covering all stages of the arbitral process.

questions.question: An action was already pending when the Federal Rules of Evidence took effect. Under their original applicability provisions, do the rules govern further procedure in that action, and what happens to the extent that applying them would not be feasible or would work injustice?

To the extent application would not be feasible or would work injustice, former evidentiary principles apply.

Ruin no more often than once in every 200 cases

questions.question: A covered company subject to the single-counterparty credit limits in 12 CFR Part 252 has $40 billion of tier 1 capital and an $11 billion aggregate net credit exposure to one counterparty. Whether the separate assessment is triggered

questions.question: A registrant's named executive officer has perquisites and personal benefits totalling $120,000, including items worth $24,000 and $26,000. questions.question: According to HMRC's rates and allowances guidance, for non-ring fence profits under the rules from 1 April 2023, is there still a single Corporation Tax rate?
