key.answer: No such Part 3 minimum applies directly to the branch, because Part 3 does not apply to Federal branches and agencies of foreign banks.

questions.commonly_confused: Answering 4.5% would wrongly apply the national bank and Federal savings association minimum to an entity expressly outside Part 3's scope.

questions.question: An institution is scoping the annual privacy notice obligation in 17 CFR Part 248, subpart A. Apart from § 248.30(b), does that subpart cover information about companies or information about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for business purposes, as in force on 2026-11-21?

sources.passage: Except with respect to § 248.30(b), this subpart applies only to nonpublic personal information about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for personal, family, or household purposes from the institutions listed below. This subpart does not apply to information about companies or about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for business, commercial, or agricultural purposes.

key.answer: No; the subpart does not apply to it.

key.item: Information about individuals obtaining products or services primarily for business purposes
key.answer: No; the subpart does not apply to it.

questions.commonly_confused: The rule that an annual notice means at least once in a 12-consecutive-month period supplies timing only; it does not bring company or business-purpose information into scope.

questions.question: An EU payment institution provides only the payment service listed in point (6) of Annex I to the EU payment-services directive adopted in 2015. Under that directive's original text, what minimum capital must it maintain at all times?

sources.passage: where the payment institution provides only the payment service as referred to in point (6) of Annex I, its capital shall at no time be less than EUR 20 000;

key.item: Minimum capital for an institution providing only the point (6) service

questions.commonly_confused: The service-specific EUR 20 000 requirement should not be replaced with capital amounts for other categories of payment institution or with a transaction-value threshold.

questions.question: Under the original text of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, by when must details of a derivative contract's conclusion, modification or termination be reported, and how long must counterparties keep records of a contract and its modifications?

sources.passage: The details shall be reported no later than the working day following the conclusion, modification or termination of the contract.
Counterparties shall keep a record of any derivative contract they have concluded and any modification for at least five years following the termination of the contract.

key.answer: No later than the working day following the contract's conclusion, modification or termination
At least five years following termination of the contract

questions.commonly_confused: Five years is the retention period after termination, not the reporting deadline, and the retention clock does not simply run for five years from the contract's conclusion.

questions.question: Under 21 CFR Part 312 as shown in the supplied eCFR text, when must a sponsor notify FDA of an unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reaction, measured from the sponsor's initial receipt of the information?

sources.passage: The sponsor must also notify FDA of any unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reaction as soon as possible but in no case later than 7 calendar days after the sponsor's initial receipt of the information.

key.answer: As soon as possible, and no later than 7 calendar days after the sponsor's initial receipt of the information.

questions.commonly_confused: A 15-calendar-day deadline is tempting because it applies to some other expedited-reporting cases, but this IND rule sets a 7-calendar-day outer limit for the stated fatal or life-threatening case.

questions.question: A person required to register its establishment under § 807.20 plans to introduce a device that requires premarket notification. Under 21 CFR Part 807 subpart E as in force on 2026-11-21, how long before the proposed introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce must the submission be made?

sources.passage: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, each person who is required to register his establishment pursuant to § 807.20 must submit a premarket notification submission to the Food and Drug Administration at least 90 days before he proposes to begin the introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce for commercial distribution of a device intended for human use which meets any of the following criteria:

key.answer: At least 90 days before the proposed introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce for commercial distribution.

questions.commonly_confused: The answer is sometimes written as 90 working days. The regulation says 90 days, without limiting them to working days.

questions.question: Under ICH E6(R2), what minimum total membership is recommended for an IRB/IEC, and which two membership characteristics should be included?

sources.passage:
It is recommended that the IRB/IEC should include: 
(a) At least five members. 
(b) At least one member whose primary area of interest is in a nonscientific area. 
(c) At least one member who is independent of the institution/trial site.

key.answer: At least 1 member whose primary area of interest is in a nonscientific area.
At least 1 member who is independent of the institution or trial site.

questions.commonly_confused: Five members with only a nonscientific representative is incomplete. The recommendation also includes at least one member independent of the institution or trial site.

questions.question: A legacy HDE checklist still quotes 4,000 individuals per year as the HUD ceiling. Under 21 CFR Part 814 as in force on 2026-11-21, what prevalence ceiling must the checklist use for the humanitarian use device definition?

sources.passage: HUD  (humanitarian use device) means a medical device intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year.

key.answer: Not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year.

questions.commonly_confused: The legacy checklist supports the tempting answer of 4,000 individuals per year, but the regulation text states not more than 8,000. The wording also includes exactly 8,000.

questions.question: Using the CDC Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Tuberculosis page available on 2026-11-21, when must the tuberculin skin test reaction be examined, and who must examine it?

sources.passage: After 48–72 hours, the skin test reaction must be examined by a trained health care worker. The health care worker measures any swelling where the tuberculin was injected to determine if the reaction to the test is positive or negative.

questions.commonly_confused: It is tempting to let the patient inspect the reaction or to wait a week. The page requires examination by a trained health care worker after 48–72 hours.

questions.question: Under 21 CFR Part 814 as in force on 2026-11-21, within how many days after FDA receives a PMA must FDA notify the applicant whether the application has been filed?

sources.passage: Within 45 days after a PMA is received by FDA, the agency will notify the applicant whether the application has been filed.

key.answer: Within 45 days after FDA receives the PMA.

questions.commonly_confused: The 180-day PMA review period is easy to substitute here, but the filing-notification passage states 45 days.

questions.question: A legacy device quality manual still cites ISO 13485:2003. Which exact ISO 13485 edition and edition date does 21 CFR Part 820 incorporate by reference as in force on 2026-11-21?

sources.passage: ISO 13485:2016(E) (“ISO 13485”), Medical devices—Quality management systems—Requirements for regulatory purposes, Third edition, March 1, 2016; IBR approved for §§ 820.1, 820.3, 820.10, 820.35, and 820.45.

questions.commonly_confused: ISO 13485:2003 is tempting because it remains in the legacy manual, but Part 820 names ISO 13485:2016(E), Third edition, March 1, 2016.

questions.question: FDA receives a De Novo request that is accepted without any additional-information submission. Under 21 CFR Part 860 as in force on 2026-11-21, what are the outside time limits for the acceptance notification and for FDA's review and granting or declining order?

sources.passage: Within 15 days after a De Novo request is received by FDA, FDA will notify the requester whether the De Novo request has been accepted.

Within 120 days after receipt of a De Novo request or receipt of additional information that results in the De Novo request being accepted under § 860.230, FDA will review the De Novo request and send the requester an order granting the De Novo request under § 860.260(a) or an order declining the De Novo request under 860.260(b).

key.answer: Within 15 days after FDA receives the De Novo request.
Within 120 days after FDA receives the request in this no-additional-information scenario.

questions.commonly_confused: Adding the periods gives a tempting 135-day answer. In this scenario, the stated 15-day and 120-day periods both run from receipt rather than sequentially.

questions.question: A sponsor first learns on day 0 that a case qualifies for ICH E2A's seven-day expedited reporting rule. What is the outer limit for notifying regulatory agencies and, if that full period is used, by what day measured from day 0 must the follow-up report that is as complete as possible be provided?

sources.passage: Regulatory agencies should be notified (e.g., by telephone, facsimile transmission, or in writing) as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies, followed by as complete a report as possible within 8 additional calendar days.

key.answer: As soon as possible, but no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor.

key.item: Follow-up report limit measured from day 0
key.answer: Day 15, or 15 calendar days after first knowledge, calculated as 7 calendar days plus 8 additional calendar days.

questions.commonly_confused: Day 8 results from measuring the additional period from day 0. The passage calls for 8 additional calendar days after the seven-day notification period, giving day 15 when the full seven days are used.

questions.question: A sponsor has submitted the initial IND and 17 later submissions, all numbered correctly under 21 CFR Part 312 as shown in the supplied eCFR text. What three-digit serial number must the next submission carry?

sources.passage: Each submission relating to an IND is required to be numbered serially using a single, three-digit serial number. The initial IND is required to be numbered 000; each subsequent submission (e.g., amendment, report, or correspondence) is required to be numbered chronologically in sequence.

key.item: Serial number of the next submission
key.answer: 018. The initial IND is 000, the 17 later submissions are 001 through 017, and the next is 018.

questions.commonly_confused: 017 is the serial number of the most recent submission, not the next one. Counting the initial IND as 001 would also shift the sequence incorrectly.

questions.question: A device meets the custom-device meaning in section 520(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Under 21 CFR Part 807 subpart E as in force on 2026-11-21, must its manufacturer submit a premarket notification at least 90 days before commercial distribution?

sources.passage: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, each person who is required to register his establishment pursuant to § 807.20 must submit a premarket notification submission to the Food and Drug Administration at least 90 days before he proposes to begin the introduction or delivery for introduction into interstate commerce for commercial distribution of a device intended for human use which meets any of the following criteria:
A custom device is exempt from premarket notification requirements of this subpart if the device is within the meaning of section 520(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

key.item: Premarket notification obligation for the stated custom device
key.answer: No. The custom-device exemption applies, so this subpart's premarket-notification requirement and its 90-day lead time do not apply.

questions.commonly_confused: Yes, 90 days before distribution, is the tempting answer because that is the general rule. It overlooks the express custom-device exemption.

questions.question: A 4-year-old who received BCG vaccine needs TB testing. On the CDC Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Tuberculosis page available on 2026-11-21, does the stated preference for TB blood tests apply to this child?

sources.passage: Only one visit is required to draw blood for the test. TB blood tests are the preferred method of TB testing for people 5 years of age and older who have received the bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine.

key.item: Applicability of the stated blood-test preference to a 4-year-old
key.answer: No. The stated preference is limited to people aged 5 years and older who received BCG; this passage does not establish that preference for a 4-year-old.

questions.commonly_confused: Yes for every BCG-vaccinated child is tempting because BCG vaccination is part of the recommendation. That reading omits the separate age condition of 5 years and older.

questions.question: A primary-care team is rewriting its pathway for identifying and treating primary hypertension in adults, including adults with type 2 diabetes. Which NICE guideline covers that scope, and which earlier NICE hypertension guideline does it say it updates and replaces?

sources.passage: This guideline covers identifying and treating primary hypertension (high blood pressure) in people aged 18 and over, including people with type 2 diabetes.
This guideline updates and replaces NICE guideline CG127. It also updates and replaces the section on blood pressure management in the NICE guideline on type 2 diabetes in adults (NG28).

key.answer: NICE NG136, Hypertension in Adults — Diagnosis and Management.

questions.commonly_confused: NG28 is tempting because the population includes adults with type 2 diabetes. NG28 is the diabetes guideline; the stated primary-hypertension scope and replacement statement identify NG136.

questions.question: An investigator says that an FDA-regulated clinical investigation may enroll a person without informed consent solely because the research is minimal risk. Under 21 CFR Part 50 as in force on 2026-11-21, is that reason sufficient, and how does the part define minimal risk?

sources.passage: Except as provided in §§ 50.22, 50.23, and 50.24, no investigator may involve a human being as a subject in research covered by these regulations unless the investigator has obtained the legally effective informed consent of the subject or the subject's legally authorized representative.

Minimal risk  means that the probability and magnitude of harm or discomfort anticipated in the research are not greater in and of themselves than those ordinarily encountered in daily life or during the performance of routine physical or psychological examinations or tests.

key.item: Whether minimal-risk status alone is sufficient to omit consent
key.answer: No. Unless an exception in §§ 50.22, 50.23, or 50.24 applies, the investigator must obtain legally effective informed consent from the subject or the subject's legally authorized representative.

The anticipated probability and magnitude of harm or discomfort are not greater in and of themselves than those ordinarily encountered in daily life or during routine physical or psychological examinations or tests.

questions.commonly_confused: Minimal risk is sometimes treated as though it automatically waived informed consent. The cited rule instead requires consent unless one of its specified exceptions applies; minimal risk is a separate risk definition.

questions.question: For a detector-calibration spreadsheet, what electron mass does the 2024 PDG Review of Particle Physics list? Give both printed values, in MeV/c² and in kg, including the parenthetical uncertainties.
questions.commonly_confused: Rounded memory values such as 0.511 MeV/c² and 9.11 × 10−31 kg omit the printed digits and uncertainties.

questions.question: In the 2024 PDG cosmic-ray review, what energy threshold defines ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs)? State whether the threshold is inclusive or exclusive.

sources.passage: CRs with energies in excess of 1EeV are referred to as ultra-high energy cosmic rays (UHECRs).

key.answer: Strictly greater than 1 EeV; the review says energies in excess of 1 EeV, so the threshold is exclusive.

questions.commonly_confused: Writing ≥ 1 EeV makes the threshold inclusive, while confusing EeV with PeV changes the energy by three orders of magnitude.

questions.question: For a preliminary Mars-lander pressure-model input, what surface pressure does the NASA Mars Fact Sheet, as available on 2026-11-21, give at mean radius? What seasonal range does it state?

sources.passage: Surface pressure:  6.36 mb at mean radius (variable from 4.0 to 8.7 mb depending on season)

questions.commonly_confused: Treating 6.36 mb as a fixed value for every season ignores the stated 4.0–8.7 mb variability; Earth's 1014 mb is a different fact-sheet entry.

questions.question: For a simple Jupiter thermal model, what temperatures does the NASA Jupiter Fact Sheet, as available on 2026-11-21, list at 1 bar and at 0.1 bar? Give the kelvin values and the Celsius values printed alongside them.

sources.passage: Temperature at 1 bar: 165 K (-108 C) Temperature at 0.1 bar: 112 K (-161 C)

questions.commonly_confused: The two pressure levels can be swapped. The Celsius figures are the fact sheet's printed rounded values, not extra decimal-precision conversions.

questions.question: In the abstract of Planck 2018 Results: Cosmological Parameters, arXiv:1807.06209, what Hubble constant is inferred assuming base-ΛCDM? Include the uncertainty and unit.

sources.passage: Assuming the base-$\Lambda$CDM cosmology, the inferred late-Universe parameters are: Hubble constant $H_0 = (67.4\pm 0.5)$km/s/Mpc; matter density parameter $\Omega_m = 0.315\pm 0.007$; and matter fluctuation amplitude $\sigma_8 = 0.811\pm 0.006$.

questions.commonly_confused: Quoting 67.4 without its ±0.5 uncertainty drops requested information; higher local-distance-ladder values are not this paper's base-ΛCDM inference.

questions.question: NASA's Earth Fact Sheet lists an equatorial radius of 6378.137 km and a polar radius of 6356.752 km. What is the equatorial-minus-polar radius difference, in km?

sources.passage:
Equatorial radius (km)	        6378.137    
Polar radius (km)               6356.752

questions.question: ESA's Gaia factsheet lists a launch mass of 2030 kg, including 400 kg of propellant. For a mass-budget audit, what percentage of the launch mass was propellant? Round to one decimal place.

sources.passage: Launch mass: 2030 kg, including 710 kg of payload, a 920 kg service module and 400 kg of propellant.

questions.commonly_confused: Dividing 400 kg by 1630 kg gives about 24.5%, but that uses launch mass with the propellant removed rather than the stated 2030 kg launch mass.

Surface density: 1.217 kg/m3
Scale height: 8.5 km
Surface pressure:  6.36 mb at mean radius (variable from 4.0 to 8.7 mb depending on season)

questions.question: An atmosphere-model code still uses the uncorrected Sutherland constant from U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976. According to NASA's errata for NTRS 19770009539, what value of S should be entered, and by how much was the document's value too small?

sources.passage: 2) The value for Sutherland's constant S is too small by 0.4.  It should be 110.4 Kelvin.

questions.commonly_confused: Subtracting 0.4 K from 110.4 K recreates the uncorrected value instead of supplying the correction. The errata explicitly says to use 110.4 K.

NASA's errata says this entry is too small by a factor of 1000. What corrected kt should be used, in J/(m·s·K), and what is the same value in W/(m·K)?

sources.passage:
However, The table III, on Page 101, 21'st row of numbers, 8'th column from left (0 meters of geometric 
altitude, Thermal Conductivity) gives: 

kt =  2.5362 * 10^(-5)  (Joules / (m . s. K)) which is too small by a factor of 1000.

key.item: Corrected value in watts per metre-kelvin

questions.question: A detector analyst wants to apply Eq. (34.5) of the 2024 PDG passage-of-particles review at βγ = 0.01 and claim the review's few-percent accuracy. Does the stated validity region support that use? Give the βγ region over which that accuracy is stated.

sources.passage: Eq. (34.5) is valid in the region 0.1 . βγ . 1000 with an accuracy of a few percent.

key.item: Whether the stated accuracy applies at βγ = 0.01
key.answer: No. βγ = 0.01 lies below the stated lower endpoint of 0.1, so that use is outside the stated validity region.
The stated region has endpoints βγ = 0.1 and βγ = 1000, with an accuracy of a few percent; βγ is dimensionless.

questions.commonly_confused: General familiarity with Bethe stopping power can tempt a yes answer, but it does not override the equation's explicit range; 0.01 is below 0.1.

questions.question: A report needs a measured neutrino-mass sum from Planck 2018. In version v4 of arXiv:1807.06209, does the result combining with BAO quote a measured value for Σmν? State exactly what constraint it gives and the confidence level the abstract assigns to upper limits.

sources.passage: [Submitted on 17 Jul 2018 (v1), last revised 9 Aug 2021 (this version, v4)]
Combining with BAO we constrain the effective extra relativistic degrees of freedom to be $N_{\rm eff} = 2.99\pm 0.17$, and the neutrino mass is tightly constrained to $\sum m_\nu< 0.12$eV.

A combined analysis gives dark matter density $\Omega_c h^2 = 0.120\pm 0.001$, baryon density $\Omega_b h^2 = 0.0224\pm 0.0001$, scalar spectral index $n_s = 0.965\pm 0.004$, and optical depth $\tau = 0.054\pm 0.007$ (in this abstract we quote $68\,\%$ confidence regions on measured parameters and $95\,\%$ on upper limits).

key.item: Whether a measured neutrino-mass sum is quoted
key.answer: No measured value is quoted; the result is an upper limit.

key.item: Neutrino-mass constraint when combining with BAO
Confidence level for upper limits in the abstract

questions.commonly_confused: The tempting answer is 0.12 eV as a measured central value, possibly with a 68% interval. It is instead an upper limit, and the abstract uses 95% confidence for upper limits.

questions.question: A magnetosphere worksheet frozen on 2026-11-21 uses the symbol Rj specifically for the Jovian model radius, not a measured mean or equatorial radius. What numerical value and unit does the public planetary reference give, and how does it define Rj?

sources.passage: Rj denotes Jovian model radius, defined here to be 71,398 km

key.answer: Rj denotes the Jovian model radius, defined as 71,398 km.

questions.commonly_confused: Substituting another tabulated Jupiter radius mixes different radius conventions; it does not answer the explicit definition of the symbol Rj.

questions.question: For detector-background budgeting, what illustration does the 2024 PDG passage-of-particles review give for the rarity of high-energy δ rays? Specifically, for a β ≈ 1 particle, how many collisions with Te > 10 keV occur on average along 90 cm of argon gas?

sources.passage: δ rays of even modest energy are rare. For a β ≈ 1 particle, for example, on average only one collision with Te > 10 keV will occur along a path length of 90 cm of argon gas [1].

key.item: Average number of collisions with Te > 10 keV
key.answer: One such collision on average along a 90 cm path in argon gas for a β ≈ 1 particle.

questions.commonly_confused: The separate statement that 90% of collisions have energy losses below 100 eV does not supply this rate; the requested illustration concerns Te > 10 keV and a 90 cm path.
